data.title: Cheetah Mobile Earnings Call Highlights AI and Robotics
data.description:
Cheetah Mobile ((CMCM)) has held its Q2 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Cheetah Mobile’s latest earnings call struck a cautiously upbeat tone despite widening losses at the group level. Executives highlighted rapid expansion in cloud and AI infrastructure, strong momentum in robotics and smart mobility, and better margins in Internet services. At the same time, they acknowledged sharp declines in advertising-related revenues and reiterated that robotics remains in an investment-heavy stage.

Total Revenue Returns to Growth

Second-quarter total revenue reached RMB 766.1 million, marking a 2.7% sequential increase and 9.9% growth versus a year earlier. Management framed this as a return to growth after prior pressure, noting that underlying businesses tied to AI, cloud and robotics are now offsetting the drag from legacy advertising operations.

Promotion

55% Off TipRanks

  • Unlock powerful investing tools with TipRanks Premium to make smarter, more confident investment decisions
  • Subscribe to TipRanks Smart Investor Newsletter, and discover new investing opportunities with data-backed stock picks
Learn more about TipRanks Premium

Cloud and AI Infrastructure Accelerate

Cloud and AI infrastructure services delivered RMB 59.1 million in revenue, up 83.1% year-over-year and 26.2% quarter-over-quarter. This fast-growing segment contributed 22.2% of total revenue, with management stressing that growth accelerated from 68% in the first quarter to 83% in the second.

Surging AI Billings and Long-Term Outlook

Gross billings for cloud and AI infrastructure exceeded RMB 500 million, more than doubling from around RMB 200 million a year ago and jumping from about RMB 300 million last quarter. Management believes billings can surpass RMB 2 billion in 2026, supported by expanding enterprise demand and a growing pipeline of AI workloads.

Enterprise AI Services and Multi-Cloud Strategy

Cheetah Mobile is positioning itself as a bridge between enterprises and large cloud providers including Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, Alibaba and Tencent. It supports deployment, cost control, training and daily operations, arguing that its differentiated service model and long relationships with cloud platforms give it a defensible niche.

Robotics Growth and Smart Mobility Launch

Revenue from Robotics and others climbed to RMB 54.5 million, rising 72.5% year-over-year and 6.4% sequential to represent 20.5% of total revenue. Management credited higher robotic-product sales volumes and the contribution from a factory acquired in late July 2025, plus initial sales of newly launched smart mobility products in Europe and China.

Smart Mobility Product Features

The company’s smart mobility devices are designed to be light, foldable and travel-friendly, weighing under 16 kilograms and offering about 10 hours of operation under certain conditions. Cheetah is combining autonomous navigation and robotics software with established electric mobility makers and wheelchair partners to accelerate adoption.

Capital-Efficient Robotics Commercialization

Executives emphasized that the smart mobility project moved from concept to initial mass production within a little over a year, with cumulative investment in only the tens of millions of RMB. By reusing existing robotics technology and partnering with manufacturers, the company aims to scale hardware without heavy capital outlays typical of full in-house development.

Shared Robotics Platform Strategy

Cheetah Mobile has built a shared robotics platform that integrates voice interaction, autonomous movement and robotic-arm functionality. Management said these capabilities are now being tailored to specific products and customer scenarios, laying groundwork that could eventually support more general-purpose robotic systems.

Internet Services Margins Improve

Adjusted operating profit in Internet services rose to RMB 25.4 million, up 14.2% year-over-year and 67.2% quarter-over-quarter. Segment margins expanded to 19.4% from 14.1% a year ago and 11.3% in the first quarter, showing that cost control and a focus on higher-quality traffic are lifting profitability even as revenue declines.

Resilient Internet Value-Added Services

Internet value-added services posted RMB 101.2 million in revenue, rising 6.7% year-over-year and 2.9% quarter-over-quarter to represent 77.6% of Internet services revenue. Management described this business as profitable, efficient and cash-generative, underscoring its role as a steady contributor amid volatility in advertising.

Underlying Growth Excluding Advertising Agency

When stripping out advertising agency services, revenue reached RMB 244.1 million, up about 10% year-over-year and 5% sequentially. The company attributed this underlying growth to continued expansion in cloud and AI infrastructure, robotics and others, and value-added Internet services, reinforcing the message of an improving business mix.

Robust Cash Position Supports Investment

As of June 30, 2026, Cheetah Mobile held CNY 1,271 million in cash and cash equivalents, or roughly USD 187.3 million. Management said this strong balance provides flexibility to invest prudently in AI and robotics opportunities, while still being mindful of capital efficiency and return expectations.

Evaluating Capital-Market Options

The company is studying a range of capital-market possibilities, including external financing, strategic investors, industrial partnerships and more independent capital operations. Management noted that any move would be calibrated to business maturity, strategic fit and regulatory and shareholder considerations, but did not commit to specific transactions.

Selective Investment in Consumer AI

Cheetah Mobile stressed that it has not walked away from consumer-facing AI products and is testing lightweight, AI-native offerings. However, executives said new consumer products will be judged on user retention and data-backed experience metrics, while enterprise AI remains the primary near-term opportunity.

Advertising Agency Revenue Under Pressure

Advertising agency services revenue fell to RMB 22.0 million, down 17% year-over-year and 15% quarter-over-quarter. The decline was linked mainly to review-policy changes at a major global advertising platform, and the segment’s share of total revenue dropped sharply to 8% from 25% a year earlier.

Operating Loss Widens Despite Mix Shift

Group operating loss widened to roughly RMB 73.6 million from RMB 28.3 million in the first quarter and RMB 11.1 million a year ago. On a non-GAAP basis, operating loss was RMB 25.6 million, still above both the prior quarter and last year’s second quarter, reflecting heavy investment in robotics and the drag from shrinking advertising activities.

Internet Services Revenue Declines

Internet services revenue fell to RMB 130.5 million, down 17.3% year-over-year and 3.4% quarter-over-quarter. Gains in Internet value-added services were not enough to fully counter a steep drop in online advertising, underscoring the structural shift away from legacy ad models.

Sharp Drop in Online Advertising Revenue

Online advertising revenue declined to RMB 29.3 million, a fall of 53.5% year-over-year and 20.2% sequentially. Management did not signal an immediate turnaround, implying that investors should view advertising as a diminishing contributor as AI and robotics become larger drivers.

Robotics Loss Narrows Year-on-Year

Robotics and others recorded an adjusted operating loss of RMB 34.0 million, narrowing by 35.5% from RMB 52.7 million a year earlier but worsening versus the previous quarter’s RMB 26.9 million. Management tied the sequential widening to ongoing investment in product development and commercialization needed to build scale.

Robotics and Smart Mobility Still Early-Stage

Executives cautioned that smart mobility and wider robotics operations are still in early investment phases and require more product iteration and sales-channel build-out. They declined to give a timeline for consistent quarterly profitability, signaling that investors should expect uneven near-term economics while the ecosystem matures.

Global Enterprise Services Profit Compression

Global Enterprise Services revenue fell 23.3% year-over-year to RMB 81.1 million, although it improved 11.5% from the prior quarter. Adjusted operating profit dropped sharply to CNY 94.3 million, down 80.7% year-over-year and 32% quarter-over-quarter, mainly due to weakness in advertising agency services, but the segment remained profit-positive.

Investor Concerns on Valuation and Liquidity

During Q&A, an analyst highlighted that Cheetah Mobile’s market value sits below its net asset value and raised issues around stock liquidity and possible strategic moves. Management acknowledged frustration over valuation and capital-market recognition and said it is monitoring options, hinting at openness to structural solutions over time.

Forward-Looking Guidance and Strategic Priorities

For 2026, management expects cloud and AI infrastructure gross billings to exceed RMB 2 billion, with related revenue above RMB 200 million, implying strong double-digit growth. The company aims to scale smart mobility shipments, move Robotics and others toward breakeven and keep Internet and Global Enterprise Services profitable and efficient, even though short-term profit is not the main priority.

Cheetah Mobile’s call painted a picture of a company in transition, leaning into cloud AI and robotics while managing the decline of its advertising legacy. For investors, the key takeaway is that growth is re-emerging in higher-quality segments, but sustained profitability will depend on how quickly the robotics and AI bets can scale and how the market ultimately rewards that shift.

data.title: ADF Group Inc. SV Earnings Call Highlights Strong Momentum
data.description:
ADF Group Inc. SV ((TSE:DRX)) has held its Q2 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

ADF Group Inc. SV used its latest earnings call to underscore a strongly positive story, even as it acknowledged margin pressures and trade uncertainty. Management highlighted surging revenue, stronger profitability, record backlog and a fortress-like cash position, framing the quarter as a turning point in scale and resilience despite tariffs, steel cost inflation and one-off accounting and FX headwinds.

Revenue Growth Accelerates on Normalized Operations

ADF posted quarterly revenue of $95 million, up $42 million from the same period last year, reflecting both volume and operational normalization. Year-to-date revenue jumped to $194.3 million from $108.5 million, a 79% surge that management linked to the end of last year’s work-sharing program at the Terrebonne plant, which had curtailed fabrication hours and sales.

Promotion

  • Subscribe to TipRanks Smart Investor Newsletter, and discover new investing opportunities with data-backed stock picks

Adjusted EBITDA and Net Income Show Strong Leverage

Profitability improved sharply, with adjusted EBITDA rising to $8.4 million from $3.7 million in the quarter as higher volumes enhanced operating leverage. Net income increased to $3 million, or $0.10 per share, versus $0.9 million, or $0.03 per share, while year-to-date earnings grew to $15 million, or $0.52 per share, from $9.6 million, or $0.34, underscoring better conversion of revenue into bottom-line results.

Margins Hold Up Year-to-Date Despite Cost Inflation

Year-to-date gross margin remained stable at 21.5% of revenue, very close to 21.3% a year earlier, as stronger volumes improved fixed-cost absorption. Management cautioned that this benefit was partly offset by higher input costs, notably steel, meaning the margin stability is notable given the inflationary backdrop rather than a sign of benign cost trends.

Customer Claim Settlement Provides Material Boost

A final settlement of a long-running claim against a Groupe LAR customer injected a meaningful one-off uplift in the quarter. The resolution generated a cumulative $20.2 million benefit to Groupe LAR’s revenue, including $5.3 million recognized by ADF Group in revenue and gross margin, enhancing reported results for both the quarter and the six-month period ended July 31, 2026.

Cash Pile Swells on Strong Operating Flow

ADF ended the quarter with cash and cash equivalents of $91.4 million, up $28.7 million from January 31, 2026, backed by robust operating cash flow of $47.1 million year-to-date. Working capital stood at $109.5 million, while the claim settlement delivered a $25 million cash inflow just before quarter-end, reinforcing the balance sheet and funding upcoming investments.

Record Backlog Underpins Multi-Year Visibility

Order backlog reached a record $693.7 million at quarter-end, including $243.3 million from Groupe LAR, providing multi-year revenue visibility. The backlog figure excludes the five-year extension option on a major long-term contract announced in July 2025, suggesting further upside to future workload beyond the reported pipeline.

Geographic Mix Tilts Toward Canada, With Flexibility

Backlog composition shifted meaningfully, with Canadian-based projects now 64% of the total compared with just 5% in April 2025, a mix management described as better suited to the current environment. Executives indicated that a roughly 50-50 split would be ideal and noted that the present 64% share is already trending toward greater diversification as new U.S. projects are added.

Expansion Projects Tracking On Time and On Budget

The Groupe LAR facility expansion in Quebec’s Lac-Saint-Jean region is advancing smoothly, with the building structure underway and key equipment ordered. Management said the project is on time and on budget, and even tracking slightly better than planned, positioning the unit to handle higher volumes and more complex work when fully ramped.

Great Falls Investment to Lift Capacity and Efficiency

ADF has begun an expansion and equipment upgrade at its Great Falls, Montana plant, aimed at boosting output and modernizing the asset base. The program is expected to add capacity, bring in newer equipment and enable operational changes that should improve efficiency, giving the company more flexibility to serve U.S. customers.

CapEx Program Backed by Solid Balance Sheet

Year-to-date capital spending of $15.5 million has funded upgrades at Terrebonne, the Groupe LAR expansion and an ERP implementation, with more investment to come. Management plans just over $40 million of full-year CapEx, including just over USD 10 million for Great Falls, and stressed that the healthy balance sheet and pending financing allow ADF to expand and modernize without straining resources.

Tariff Relief Limits Impact of Latest Measures

Executives emphasized that newly announced 50% U.S. tariffs are not hitting ADF’s products, easing fears of an immediate shock. The company also expects relief from Canadian counter-tariffs that became effective earlier in the week, and based on information available at the time of the call, it saw no direct impact from recent U.S. presidential proclamations on its current operations.

Dividend Signals Confidence in Cash Generation

The board approved a second semiannual dividend of $0.02 per share, payable in mid-October to shareholders of record in late September, extending a modest but consistent payout. While the yield is small, the decision underscores management’s confidence in the company’s cash generation and balance sheet strength amid an elevated investment cycle.

SG&A Discipline Supports Operating Leverage

Management reiterated that core SG&A, excluding share-based units, should remain broadly stable as revenue and backlog grow, reinforcing operating leverage. The only notable planned increase is annual salary growth around 3%, suggesting ADF expects to scale volumes and projects without a corresponding step-up in overhead costs.

CFO Transition Designed to Be Seamless

The search for a successor to retiring CFO Jean-François Boursier is progressing well, with an announcement anticipated shortly. Boursier will stay on as CFO through year-end 2026 and then move into a strategic adviser role, a staged transition that aims to preserve financial discipline and continuity during a period of rapid expansion.

Quarterly Margin Slips on Tariffs and Steel Costs

Second-quarter gross margin declined to 18.7% of revenue from 20.7% a year earlier, as higher steel prices and recent tariff changes eroded the benefit of stronger volumes. Management acknowledged that these pressures weighed on profitability in the short term, even though structural improvement in scale and utilization remains intact.

Share-Unit Charges and FX Losses Hit Earnings

Accounting for DSUs, PSUs and RSUs reduced net earnings by $4.3 million, or $0.15 per share, in the quarter and $5.6 million, or $0.20 per share, year-to-date, largely due to mark-to-market effects from rising stock prices. Foreign exchange losses added further noise, cutting net earnings by $1.8 million, or $0.06 per share, in the quarter and $1.4 million, or $0.05 per share, over six months.

Legacy Groupe LAR Backlog Still Dragging Margins

Management cautioned that Groupe LAR’s existing backlog is booked at below ADF’s historical margin levels and will continue to weigh on results through the third and fourth quarters. As these legacy contracts are completed, executives expect margins to improve, making the current drag a temporary but visible headwind in reported profitability.

Tariffs and Steel Costs Remain Structural Headwinds

ADF noted that it cannot fully escape U.S. tariffs, and since April 2026 it has been paying roughly 10% of the commercial invoice on Canadian fabrication for U.S. projects, compressing margins on those orders. Higher steel costs also inflate the cost base, meaning even strong backlog and utilization must work harder to protect profitability.

Trade Environment Adds a Layer of Uncertainty

While the latest tariff moves and proclamations have limited direct impact so far, management said they clearly heighten uncertainty for planning and bidding. The company acknowledged that future developments are unknown, and that navigating shifting policy and trade rules will remain a key challenge in forecasting margins and project economics.

Backlog Mix Gradually Shifts Toward U.S. Work

Although Canada still accounts for 64% of the backlog, that share has already eased from 72% at the end of the first quarter as recent announcements were mainly U.S.-based projects. The evolving mix suggests ADF is steadily rebuilding its U.S. presence, which could provide natural currency and market diversification over time, albeit under a more complex tariff regime.

Guidance Points to Stable Margins and Controlled Costs

Looking ahead, management said full-year CapEx should come in just above $40 million, with just over USD 10 million earmarked for Great Falls. They view the current 21.5% year-to-date gross margin as a solid indication of near-term performance and expect margins to creep higher in the third and fourth quarters as lower-margin Groupe LAR backlog rolls off, while the 10% tariff burden on certain Canadian-to-U.S. work remains built into expectations and SG&A stays broadly stable aside from 3% wage inflation.

ADF Group’s earnings call painted a picture of a company scaling up with record backlog, strong cash and disciplined spending, even as tariffs and legacy contracts compress margins. For investors, the key takeaway is that growth and operational leverage are firmly in place, and management expects gradual margin improvement, making near-term volatility more a function of transitory headwinds than fundamental weakness.

Positive Start to the Second Half

Momentum has carried into the second half, with store and online sales in constant currency up 9% between 1 August and 7 September 2026 versus a year earlier. Management said Autumn/Winter collections are being very well received, suggesting demand remains firm as the key season ramps up.

Resilient Gross Profit and Profitability

Gross profit increased 8.3% to EUR 11.6 billion, delivering a gross margin of 58.7% despite higher transport costs. EBITDA grew 7.8% to EUR 5.5 billion and profit before tax rose 6.8% to EUR 3.8 billion, with a PBT margin of 19.5% and broadly stable EBITDA and EBIT margins.

Strong Cash Generation and Financial Position

Funds from operations jumped 11% to EUR 4.1 billion, highlighting the strength of the business model. Inditex reported a net cash position above EUR 10 billion, giving the company ample financial flexibility to fund investments and cushion against market volatility.

Global Reach and Diversified Operating Model

Inditex now operates eight concepts in 98 markets, moving to 99 with its first store in Curaçao, and has online operations in 215 markets. All geographic areas delivered positive sales evolution in constant currency, underscoring the benefits of a highly diversified footprint.

Integrated Store and Online Channels

Around 60% of online returns are processed through stores and roughly 20% of online orders are collected in-store, showing deep integration between channels. Management said this omnichannel model improves demand visibility and inventory management, while enhancing the overall customer experience.

Flexible Supply Chain and Supplier Relationships

Production is spread across more than 50 markets and sourcing spans nearly 50 origins, limiting concentration risk. Over 70% of production volume is backed by supplier relationships longer than eight years, supported by 16 logistics centers that operate as a single inventory with multimodal transport.

Long-Term Growth Opportunity

Management estimates Inditex holds only about 2% global market share across its concepts, leaving substantial room for expansion. Non-Zara concepts have limited commercial presence in 59 markets, where at least one brand generates under EUR 50 million in annual sales, highlighting a clear runway.

Growth of Younger Concepts

Three younger banners delivered sales well above EUR 1 billion at the half-year mark, cementing their role in the portfolio. Bershka posted a 12% sales CAGR from 2022 to first-half 2026, while Stradivarius delivered a 15% CAGR over the same period, pointing to strong brand traction.

Retail Optimization and Online Expansion

Physical gross space has grown at a 5% compound annual rate over the last three years, supported by retail optimization in 51 markets. Online sales have expanded more than 18% per year on average since 2019, showing that digital remains a powerful growth engine.

Continued Store and Geographic Expansion

Recent openings include Bershka’s first U.S. store in Miami Aventura and a second Brazil store in Rio Barra, plus Stradivarius’s first Munich location. Massimo Dutti opened its first street-level store in Seoul Hannam and Lefties its first U.K. store in Liverpool, with further launches planned in London, Newcastle and New York.

Investment in Technology and Customer Experience

Inditex is rolling out soft tag technology across all stores alongside Click & Collect silos, assisted checkouts, drop-off points and automated sorters. Online, the group is developing personalization and communities and has launched initiatives such as Zara Try-on, Zara Man standalone stores, footwear showrooms and BSK MMBRS.

Ongoing Investment to Support Future Growth

Ordinary CapEx reached EUR 1.3 billion in the first half, with around EUR 2.3 billion planned for 2026 as a whole. Investment focuses on the global store base, online platforms, tech integration and process efficiency, plus roughly EUR 200 million of extraordinary CapEx for corporate facilities including a new Barcelona campus.

Sustainability and Community Partnerships

Inditex highlighted several partnerships with global organizations to support social and environmental goals. Initiatives include Amazon Forest protection and restoration and aid efforts that improve conditions for vulnerable communities and respond to natural disasters.

Higher Transport and Input Costs

Disruptions in the Middle East drove elevated transport and input costs in the first half, weighing on profitability. Management said these higher transport costs hit both gross margin and operating expenses, but remain manageable within current guidance.

Operating Expenses Grew Faster Than Sales

Operating expenses rose 8.3% in the first six months of 2026, outpacing the 7.6% sales increase and causing mild margin deleverage. The company linked this mainly to higher transport spending and incremental costs tied to online fulfillment and distribution to franchisees.

Expected Second-Half Gross Margin Impact

Due to a lag between transport cost spikes and their reflection in cost of goods sold, management expects some gross margin pressure in the second half. Even so, Inditex reiterated full-year guidance for a stable gross margin within plus or minus 50 basis points, signaling confidence.

Middle East Sales Remain Affected

Geopolitical tensions continue to dampen sales in the Middle East, although trends have improved versus the first quarter. The company has around 480 franchise-operated stores in the region and reported that all locations are open, suggesting operational resilience.

Reduced FX Sourcing Tailwind

A weaker U.S. dollar delivered a modest FX sourcing benefit in the first half, lowering some input costs. Based on current data, management now expects this tailwind to fade and be neutral in the second half, removing a minor boost to margins.

Ongoing Geopolitical and Market Uncertainty

Executives flagged broader geopolitical uncertainty and market volatility, with particular reference to the Middle East conflict. They stressed that the situation remains sensitive and will be closely monitored, but affirmed that the business model is built to absorb shocks.

Forward-Looking Guidance and Outlook

For 2026, Inditex reiterated expectations for a minus 1% top line currency impact and a gross margin held within plus or minus 50 basis points. The group plans around EUR 2.3 billion in ordinary CapEx, nearly EUR 200 million in extraordinary CapEx and roughly 5% annual gross space growth with positive net space and strong online expansion, while keeping operating margins broadly stable.

Inditex’s earnings call painted a picture of a highly profitable, cash-rich retailer investing aggressively in growth, technology and sustainability. While transport costs, margin headwinds and geopolitical risks remain on the radar, management’s tone and guidance suggest investors can expect continued disciplined expansion and resilient performance.

data.title: B3 Grants Renova Energia Extra Time to Meet Free Float Rules
data.description:
The latest announcement is out from Renova Energia S.A. ( (BR:RNEW3) ).

Renova Energia S.A. announced that B3, the Brazilian stock exchange, has granted an automatic and extraordinary extension for the company to meet the minimum free float requirement under the Level 2 listing rules. The new deadline to comply with the required percentage of shares in circulation has been pushed out to December 31, 2027, giving Renova more time to adjust its shareholder base and preserve its Level 2 listing status.

This extension reflects B3’s consideration of the current macroeconomic environment and eases immediate pressure on Renova to restructure its free float. The decision may help stabilize the company’s market positioning and provide additional flexibility for capital markets strategies, with implications for existing shareholders and potential investors who rely on the governance standards associated with B3’s Level 2 segment.
